summary: @servicetitan/help-center ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, unzips it, chmods it executable, and uses execFileSync to invoke the downloaded Bun binary against the sibling file math_init.js at npm install time. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line bundle with hex-named identifiers, a rotating-index string-array decoder (WV8StW pattern), and a '// @bun @bun-cjs' banner indicating it is compiled for the Bun runtime the preinstall step just downloaded. The obfuscated payload is not referenced by the advertised React help-center library entrypoint (dist/index.js) and has no functional relationship to the advertised component library. Bun is fetched from its official project domain, but it is used solely to bootstrap execution of an in-tree obfuscated payload rather than to build or run the advertised library — the alternate-runtime dropper pattern, used to evade Node-based install-time scanners. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope with a matching repository URL, creating the appearance of first-party ServiceTitan tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
